posts.title: Grandma’s Turnip Curry
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Grandma’s Turnip Curry turns a large quantity of turnips into a soft, mashable curry with cumin, onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and cayenne.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.203
posts.body_markdown:
Grandma’s Turnip Curry turns a large quantity of turnips into a soft, mashable curry with cumin, onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and cayenne.

The turnips cook covered with only a small amount of water, so they soften in the seasoned base rather than boiling in a large volume of liquid. The source suggests adding more water only if the pan needs it.

Maple syrup is stirred in at the end before the turnips are mashed. That small sweet note balances the earthy flavor of the turnips without making the dish dessert-like.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons good oil
- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1 small onion, chopped
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 8 cups large turnips, peeled and cubed
- 1/4 cup water
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon sea salt
- Cayenne pepper to taste
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup

## Method
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Add the turnips, water, turmeric, salt, and cayenne and toss to combine. Reduce to medium, cover, and cook for 30–40 minutes until the turnips are soft, adding a little more water if needed. Stir in the maple syrup, mash the turnips, adjust the seasoning, and serve. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Sweet & Sour Sambaro
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Sweet & Sour Sambaro is a cabbage-and-carrot condiment with mustard seeds, dried and fresh chilies, turmeric, gur, and lemon.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.204
posts.body_markdown:
Sweet & Sour Sambaro is a cabbage-and-carrot condiment with mustard seeds, dried and fresh chilies, turmeric, gur, and lemon. The vegetables stay lightly cooked rather than soft.

The cabbage is salted and pressed before cooking, then rinsed and squeezed dry. That preliminary step removes moisture and helps the finished sambaro keep a firmer texture.

The sweet and sour notes are added at the very end with gur and lemon juice. The pan comes off the heat immediately afterward so the cabbage and carrots do not continue to cook.

## Ingredients
- 3 cups cabbage, chopped
- 1 tablespoon salt, for sweating
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 2 dried red chilies
- 1/2 teaspoon black mustard seeds
- 1/2 cup carrots, julienned
- 2 fresh green chilies, slit at the end
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 tablespoon gur
- Juice of 1 lemon
- Salt to taste

## Method
Place the cabbage in a colander, sprinkle with the tablespoon of salt, set a plate and heavy can on top, and leave it to sweat for 1–2 hours. Rinse and squeeze out excess moisture. Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat, add the dried chilies, and cook until darkened. Add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the cabbage, carrots, green chilies, and turmeric and sauté for 3–4 minutes. Add the gur and lemon juice and cook for another 1–2 minutes until the gur dissolves. Remove from the heat, transfer to a serving bowl, adjust the salt, and remove the whole chilies before serving. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Spicy Tomato Pasta
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Spicy Tomato Pasta is a quick tomato sauce built while the pasta cooks. Onion, garlic, green chili, tomato, and cilantro or basil provide the main flavor.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.206
posts.body_markdown:
Spicy Tomato Pasta is a quick tomato sauce built while the pasta cooks. Onion, garlic, green chili, tomato, and cilantro or basil provide the main flavor.

The tomatoes are cooked only until softened, keeping the sauce fresh rather than long-simmered. Salt and pepper are added after the tomatoes have broken down enough to coat the pasta.

Parmesan is used as the final garnish. The source also offers basil, goat feta, olives, and capers as variations, but the base version stays focused on tomato and cilantro.

## Ingredients
- 2–4 cups uncooked pasta of your choice, about 1 cup per serving
- 2 teaspoons olive oil
- 1/4 cup onions, chopped
- 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 2–3 teaspoons fresh green chilies, minced
- 4 cups Roma tomatoes, chopped with their juices
- 1/2–1 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- Salt to taste
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- Parmesan cheese, grated, to taste

## Method
Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water until al dente. While it cooks, heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the onions and sauté for 2–3 minutes, then add the garlic and chilies and cook for another 1–2 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring often, for 4–5 minutes until softened. Reduce to medium, stir in the cilantro, salt, and pepper, and cook for 1 minute. Drain the pasta and serve it with the tomato sauce and grated Parmesan. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Amrita’s Pasta
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Amrita’s Pasta is a no-cook toss once the pasta is ready, combining artichoke hearts, sun-dried tomatoes, feta, pine nuts, optional black olives.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.207
posts.body_markdown:
Amrita’s Pasta is a no-cook toss once the pasta is ready, combining artichoke hearts, sun-dried tomatoes, feta, pine nuts, optional black olives, and fresh basil.

The artichoke hearts are added with their liquid, which helps dress the pasta without needing a separate sauce. Sun-dried tomatoes and feta bring concentrated savory flavor.

Pine nuts and herbs are folded through at the end so they keep their texture and aroma. The dish is designed to be served with a fresh salad.

## Ingredients
- 8 cups penne or farfalle pasta, cooked al dente
- 1 jar artichoke hearts with liquid, about 16 ounces
- 2–3 tablespoons sun-dried tomatoes in oil
- 1/2–3/4 cup feta cheese, crumbled
- 1/3 cup pine nuts, lightly toasted
- 1/3 cup black olives, chopped, optional
- 1/2–1 cup fresh basil, chopped
- Salt to taste
- Freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Place the cooked pasta in a large bowl. Add the artichoke hearts and their liquid, sun-dried tomatoes, feta, toasted pine nuts, optional black olives, and basil. Toss gently until the ingredients are evenly distributed and the pasta is lightly coated with the artichoke liquid. Season with salt and freshly ground pepper to taste and serve. Makes 6 servings.

posts.title: Kamut Spaghetti with Cilantro Pesto
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Kamut Spaghetti with Cilantro Pesto | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Kamut Spaghetti with Cilantro Pesto replaces a traditional basil pesto with a cilantro-forward sauce.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.208
posts.body_markdown:
Kamut Spaghetti with Cilantro Pesto replaces a traditional basil pesto with a cilantro-forward sauce. Parsley, pine nuts, Parmesan, olive oil, and sun-dried tomatoes round out the pesto.

Garlic and optional green chili are minced first in the blender or food processor. The herbs are pulsed next, followed by the remaining ingredients until the mixture becomes a smooth paste.

The sauce is tossed with hot, drained spaghetti rather than cooked in a separate pan. This keeps the fresh-herb character of the pesto intact.

## Ingredients
- Kamut spaghetti, enough for 4–6 people
- 3–4 teaspoons garlic
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh green chilies, optional
- 3 cups fresh cilantro leaves, packed
- 3/4 cup fresh parsley, packed
- 1/2 cup pine nuts
- 1/2 cup olive oil
- 3/4 cup Parmesan cheese, grated
- 1/4 cup sun-dried tomatoes in oil
- Salt to taste

## Method
Cook the Kamut spaghetti in boiling water until al dente. While it cooks, combine the garlic and optional green chili in a blender or food processor and pulse until minced. Add the cilantro and parsley and pulse again. Add the pine nuts, olive oil, Parmesan, sun-dried tomatoes, and salt and blend until a smooth pesto forms. Drain the spaghetti, toss thoroughly with the cilantro pesto, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Spaghetti with Garlic & Red Chili Peppers
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Spaghetti with Garlic & Red Chili Peppers | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Spaghetti with Garlic & Red Chili Peppers is a minimal pasta dish in which sliced garlic and whole dried chilies flavor a mixture of olive oil and ghee.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.209
posts.body_markdown:
Spaghetti with Garlic & Red Chili Peppers is a minimal pasta dish in which sliced garlic and whole dried chilies flavor a mixture of olive oil and ghee.

The garlic is cooked only until it begins to brown, while the dried chilies darken and perfume the oil. The source leaves the whole chilies in the pasta for flavor but notes that they are not meant to be eaten.

Cooked spaghetti is tossed directly into the seasoned fat, then finished with salt, pepper, and grated Parmesan.

## Ingredients
- Spaghetti, cooked al dente, enough for 4–6 people
- 1–2 teaspoons olive oil
- 1–2 teaspoons ghee or butter
- 3 whole dried red chilies
- 6–8 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese, grated

## Method
Heat the olive oil and ghee in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the whole dried chilies and sliced garlic and sauté, tossing regularly, until the garlic begins to brown and the chilies darken. Add the cooked spaghetti and toss until evenly coated with the seasoned oil. Add salt and freshly ground pepper to taste, sprinkle with Parmesan, and serve. Remove the whole chilies before eating if preferred. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Mushroom, Leek & Red Bell Pepper Quiche
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Mushroom, Leek & Red Bell Pepper Quiche | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Mushroom, Leek & Red Bell Pepper Quiche fills two prepared pie crusts with sautéed vegetables, Gruyere, and a lightly seasoned egg custard.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.211
posts.body_markdown:
Mushroom, Leek & Red Bell Pepper Quiche fills two prepared pie crusts with sautéed vegetables, Gruyere, and a lightly seasoned egg custard.

Onion, leek, mushrooms, and red pepper are cooked with thyme, salt, ghee, and olive oil, then cooled. The egg mixture is whisked separately with milk, flour, salt, and dry mustard.

Cheese goes into the crust before the vegetables and custard, with cayenne sprinkled over the top. The quiches bake until set in the center but not hard.

## Ingredients
- 2 pre-made pie crusts
- 1 teaspoon ghee or butter
- 1 teaspoon olive oil
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 1 leek, sliced, white parts only
- 3 cups mushrooms, sliced
- 1/4 cup red bell peppers, finely diced
- Salt to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon thyme
- 4 eggs
- 1 1/2 cups milk
- 3 tablespoons unbleached white flour
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon dry mustard
- 1 1/2 cups Gruyere cheese, grated
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper

## Method
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Heat the ghee and olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the onions and leeks and sauté for 2–3 minutes, then add the mushrooms, bell pepper, salt, and thyme and cook for 3–5 minutes. Cool the vegetables. In a mixing bowl, beat the eggs, milk, flour, salt, and dry mustard until well blended and slightly foamy. Divide the Gruyere between the two pie crusts, spread the cooled vegetables over the cheese, and pour half the egg mixture into each crust. Sprinkle with cayenne and bake for 40–45 minutes, until set in the center. Makes 2 medium quiches, about 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Crustless Quiche with Mushrooms, Leeks & Red Bell Peppers
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Crustless Quiche with Mushrooms, Leeks & Red Bell Peppers | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Crustless Quiche with Mushrooms, Leeks & Red Bell Peppers uses the same vegetable and egg filling as the preceding quiche but leaves out the pastry crust.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.212
posts.body_markdown:
Crustless Quiche with Mushrooms, Leeks & Red Bell Peppers uses the same vegetable and egg filling as the preceding quiche but leaves out the pastry crust.

The vegetables are sautéed and cooled before being mixed directly into the beaten egg, milk, flour, mustard, and salt mixture. This changes the assembly but keeps the flavor profile of the original.

The mixture is baked in a lightly oiled pie pan with Gruyere on top and a final sprinkle of cayenne. The cheese is allowed to bubble and turn golden as the center sets.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon ghee or butter
- 1 teaspoon olive oil
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 1 leek, sliced, white parts only
- 3 cups mushrooms, sliced
- 1/4 cup red bell peppers, finely diced
- Salt to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon thyme
- 4 eggs
- 1 1/2 cups milk
- 3 tablespoons unbleached white flour
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon dry mustard
- 1 1/2 cups Gruyere cheese, grated
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper

## Method
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Sauté the onions and leeks in the ghee and olive oil for 2–3 minutes, then add the mushrooms, bell pepper, salt, and thyme and cook 3–5 minutes. Let the vegetables cool. Beat the eggs, milk, flour, salt, and dry mustard until blended and slightly foamy, then mix in the cooled vegetables. Pour into a lightly oiled pie pan, spread the Gruyere evenly over the top, sprinkle with cayenne, and bake for 35–40 minutes until the center is set and the cheese is bubbling and golden. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Curried Eggs
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Curried Eggs pairs hard-boiled eggs with a slow-cooked onion and tomato curry. The eggs are added only after the sauce is fully seasoned and softened.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.213
posts.body_markdown:
Curried Eggs pairs hard-boiled eggs with a slow-cooked onion and tomato curry. The eggs are added only after the sauce is fully seasoned and softened.

Onion and turmeric cook gently until the onion turns golden. Tomato, cayenne, and salt then simmer under a lid before lemon juice is added.

The halved eggs are placed into the sauce carefully so the yolks stay intact. Garam masala and parsley or cilantro finish the dish just before serving.

## Ingredients
- 4 eggs, hard-boiled and halved
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 2 cups tomatoes, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
- Salt to taste
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/4 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley or cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-low heat. Add the onions and turmeric and sauté, stirring often, until the onions turn golden, about 8–10 minutes. Increase the heat to medium, add the tomatoes, cayenne, and salt, cover, and cook for 8–10 minutes until the tomatoes soften. Stir in the lemon juice. Gently add the halved eggs, keeping the yolks intact, and spoon the tomato curry over them. Sprinkle with garam masala, garnish with parsley or cilantro, and serve. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Spiced “Buttermilk” Curry
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Spiced "Buttermilk" Curry is a yogurt-and-gram-flour curry with mustard seeds, cumin, fenugreek, curry leaves, ginger, garlic, and warming spices.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.214
posts.body_markdown:
Spiced “Buttermilk” Curry is a yogurt-and-gram-flour curry with mustard seeds, cumin, fenugreek, curry leaves, ginger, garlic, and warming spices.

The yogurt, water, and gram flour are whisked smooth before they meet the hot spice mixture. Once added to the pot, the sauce is stirred continuously as it comes to a boil to keep the texture even.

Gur, salt, cayenne, and lemon juice are added only after the curry thickens. The final consistency is similar to whipping cream, and cilantro is used as the garnish.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/4 cups plain yogurt
- 1 1/2 cups water
- 2 tablespoons gram flour
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- 1/2 teaspoon mustard seeds
- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1/4 teaspoon fenugreek seeds
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end
- 3–5 curry leaves
- 2 cloves
- 1/2 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon gur or other sweetener
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Whisk the yogurt, water, and gram flour in a bowl until smooth. Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat, add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, green chili, curry leaves, cloves, garlic, ginger, and turmeric and sauté for 30 seconds. Pour in the yogurt mixture while stirring or whisking continuously and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring, until thickened to the consistency of whipping cream. Add the gur and stir until dissolved, then add salt, cayenne, and lemon juice. Remove any whole spices if desired, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 2–3 servings.

posts.title: Whole Wheat Chapatis
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Whole Wheat Chapatis are simple unleavened flatbreads made from whole wheat flour, salt, ghee or oil, and boiling water.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.218
posts.body_markdown:
Whole Wheat Chapatis are simple unleavened flatbreads made from whole wheat flour, salt, ghee or oil, and boiling water. The dough is kneaded twice before being divided and rolled.

Each chapati is cooked in a dry heavy pan rather than baked. Pressing the edges as bubbles form helps the bread trap steam and puff while it cooks.

The finished chapatis are stacked and covered so they stay warm and do not dry out. The source notes that practice improves the evenness of rolling and puffing.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups whole wheat flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, optional
- 1 1/2 tablespoons ghee or good oil
- 1 cup boiling water, plus a little more if needed

## Method
Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the ghee and mix with your hands, then pour in the boiling water and stir with a wooden spoon. Let the mixture cool enough to handle, knead into a firm smooth dough, cover for 5 minutes, then knead again for 4–5 minutes. Divide into 10 balls. Roll each ball on a lightly floured surface into a 7-inch circle. Cook each chapati in a dry heavy-bottomed or non-stick pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute per side, pressing the edges gently when bubbles appear to encourage puffing. Stack the cooked chapatis in a covered warm dish, separating with wax paper or a little ghee if desired. Makes 10 chapatis.

posts.title: Spelt Chapatis
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Spelt Chapatis adapt the basic flatbread method to spelt flour, which needs slightly less liquid than wheat flour and benefits from gentle handling.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.220
posts.body_markdown:
Spelt Chapatis adapt the basic flatbread method to spelt flour, which needs slightly less liquid than wheat flour and benefits from gentle handling.

The dough is mixed with warm water, rested briefly, then kneaded again after melted ghee is poured over it. This produces a firm, smooth dough before shaping.

The chapatis are rolled thin and cooked one at a time in a dry pan. Once cooked, they are stacked and covered to keep them soft until serving.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups spelt flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 cup warm water
- 1 1/2 tablespoons ghee, melted, or good oil

## Method
Combine the spelt flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the warm water and mix with your hands, then knead into a firm smooth dough. If the dough is sticky, add flour 1 tablespoon at a time; if dry, add water in the same way. Cover and rest for 5 minutes. Pour the melted ghee over the dough and knead again. Divide into 10 balls and roll each on a lightly floured surface into a 7-inch circle. Cook each chapati in a dry heavy-bottomed or non-stick pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute per side, pressing the edges gently as bubbles form. Stack the cooked chapatis in a covered dish and keep warm. Makes 10 chapatis.

posts.title: Corn Chapatis
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Corn Chapatis are rustic flatbreads made from corn flour and cooked cornmeal, with ghee and optional yogurt adding enough richness to bind the dough.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.221
posts.body_markdown:
Corn Chapatis are rustic flatbreads made from corn flour and cooked cornmeal, with ghee and optional yogurt adding enough richness to bind the dough.

Because the dough is more fragile than wheat dough, the source shapes the rounds with oiled hands rather than relying entirely on a rolling pin.

Each chapati cooks for several minutes on both sides in a dry pan. The finished breads are stacked and covered so they remain warm and do not dry out.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup ground corn flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon ghee or olive oil
- 1 tablespoon plain yogurt, optional
- 1/2 cup cornmeal, cooked
- 1/2 cup cold water, plus more if needed

## Method
Combine the corn flour, salt, ghee, and optional yogurt in a large bowl. Add the cooked cornmeal and mix again. Add the cold water 1 tablespoon at a time and knead until a dough forms, adding more corn flour if too moist or more water if too dry. Divide into 6 balls. Rub your hands with a little oil and shape each ball on a lightly floured surface into a flat 5-inch circle. Cook each chapati in a dry heavy-bottomed or non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side. Stack the cooked chapatis in a covered ovenproof dish, separating with wax paper or a little ghee if desired. Makes 6 chapatis.

posts.title: Spelt & Gram Flour Chapatis
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Spelt & Gram Flour Chapatis combine equal parts spelt and gram flour with cilantro, buttermilk, and a little oil.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.222
posts.body_markdown:
Spelt & Gram Flour Chapatis combine equal parts spelt and gram flour with cilantro, buttermilk, and a little oil. The mixture makes a flavorful, filling flatbread.

The dough is kneaded until smooth, then divided into six balls and rolled into thin circles. If it becomes sticky, extra spelt flour is added a tablespoon at a time.

Like the other chapatis in the source, these cook quickly in a dry pan and are kept covered afterward. The source suggests yogurt or curry as natural accompaniments.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup gram flour
- 1/2 cup spelt flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 tablespoon buttermilk
- 1 teaspoon good oil

## Method
Combine the gram flour, spelt flour, salt, and cilantro in a large bowl. Add the water, buttermilk, and oil and knead until a smooth dough forms. If the dough is too sticky, add more spelt flour 1 tablespoon at a time. Divide into 6 balls and roll each on a lightly floured surface into a 6–7-inch circle. Cook each chapati in a dry heavy-bottomed or non-stick pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute per side, pressing the edges gently as bubbles form. Stack the cooked chapatis in a covered dish and keep warm until serving. Makes 6 chapatis.

posts.title: Ugali
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Ugali is a firm cooked maize preparation and a staple in Kenyan meals.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.223
posts.body_markdown:
Ugali is a firm cooked maize preparation and a staple in Kenyan meals. The source serves it alongside African Spinach or vegetable, bean, and lentil curries.

The flour is whisked gradually into boiling salted water to avoid lumps. As it cooks, the mixture thickens until it pulls away cleanly from the sides of the pot.

A short rest before serving lets the texture settle. White maize flour is the traditional choice, though the source allows grits, sorghum, or yellow cornmeal as substitutes.

## Ingredients
- 4 cups water
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste, optional
- 2 cups white maize flour, or grits, sorghum, or yellow cornmeal

## Method
Bring the water and optional salt to a boil in a pot over high heat. Add the maize flour 1 tablespoon at a time while whisking constantly so no lumps form. Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue cooking and stirring until the mixture becomes thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot, about 5–6 minutes. Let it sit for about 5 minutes, remove from the heat, rest for another minute, and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Alu Roti
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Alu Roti are stuffed whole-wheat flatbreads filled with seasoned mashed potatoes.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.224
posts.body_markdown:
Alu Roti are stuffed whole-wheat flatbreads filled with seasoned mashed potatoes. The method has three stages: making the dough, preparing the filling, and rolling and cooking the stuffed rounds.

The potato filling combines onion, cumin, garam masala, green chili, cilantro, and lemon. It is cooled enough to handle before being enclosed inside individual pieces of dough.

Each stuffed roti is rolled again after sealing, then cooked on a dry griddle with melted ghee brushed on both sides. The breads are served hot.

## Ingredients
- 4 cups whole wheat flour
- 9 tablespoons ghee
- 1 cup cold water
- 3 medium potatoes, peeled and quartered
- 3 tablespoons good oil
- 1/2 cup onions, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/4–1/2 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves, minced
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/4 cup ghee, melted, for brushing

## Method
For the dough, mix the flour and ghee with your hands until crumbly, add the cold water, and knead to a firm smooth dough, adding more water if needed. Cover and rest for 30 minutes. For the filling, boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash them. Sauté the onions in oil for 4–5 minutes, add salt, cumin, garam masala, chili, and mashed potatoes, then remove from the heat and stir in cilantro and lemon juice. Divide the dough into 12 balls and roll each into a 5-inch circle. Place one-twelfth of the filling in the center, fold and pinch closed, flatten, then gently roll to a 6-inch circle. Cook each roti in a dry pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, flip, brush with ghee, cook 2 minutes, flip again, brush the second side, and cook 1 minute more until lightly browned. Makes 12 roti.

posts.title: Mooli Roti
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Mooli Roti uses the same stuffed-flatbread technique as alu roti but replaces the potato filling with grated daikon, chili, cilantro, ginger, and lemon.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.226
posts.body_markdown:
Mooli Roti uses the same stuffed-flatbread technique as alu roti but replaces the potato filling with grated daikon, chili, cilantro, ginger, and lemon.

The dough is made from whole wheat flour, ghee, and cold water and rests for thirty minutes before shaping. The fresh filling is mixed separately and does not require precooking.

Each roti is stuffed, sealed, gently rolled again, and cooked on a dry pan with melted ghee brushed onto both sides. The source pairs it with yogurt and chutney.

## Ingredients
- 4 cups whole wheat flour
- 9 tablespoons ghee
- 1 cup cold water
- 3 cups daikon, grated
- 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
- 1 1/2 teaspoons fresh green chilies, minced, or to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1 1/2 teaspoons fresh ginger, minced
- 1 tablespoon lemon juice
- 1/4 cup ghee, melted, for brushing

## Method
Mix the flour and ghee until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Add the cold water and knead until a firm smooth dough forms, adding more water a tablespoon at a time if needed. Cover and rest for 30 minutes. Mix the grated daikon, salt, chili, cilantro, ginger, and lemon juice in a bowl. Divide the dough into 12 balls and roll each into a 5-inch circle. Place one-twelfth of the filling in the center, fold the edges over, pinch closed, flatten, and gently roll to a 6-inch circle. Cook each roti in a dry pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, flip, brush with ghee, cook 2 minutes, flip again, brush the second side, and cook about 1 minute more until lightly browned. Makes 12 rotis.

posts.title: Traditional Rotlo
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Traditional Rotlo is a dense millet flatbread made with flour, salt, oil or ghee, and cold water.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.228
posts.body_markdown:
Traditional Rotlo is a dense millet flatbread made with flour, salt, oil or ghee, and cold water. Its dough is intentionally much softer and more clay-like than chapati dough.

The shaped round is thicker and more fragile, so the source recommends lifting it with a broad spatula to keep it from breaking before it reaches the pan.

Rotlo does not puff. It is cooked until both sides are crisp and brown, then cut into quarters for serving.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/4 cups millet flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 2 teaspoons grapeseed oil, olive oil, or ghee
- 1/4 cup cold water, plus more if needed

## Method
Combine all the ingredients in a large bowl and knead with your hands until the dough has the consistency of wet clay. If it is too dry, add water 1 tablespoon at a time; if too soft, add more millet flour. On a lightly floured surface, flatten the dough with a rolling pin or your palms into an 8-inch circle. If it cracks, wet your fingers and press it back together. Lift the round with a wide spatula and cook in a dry heavy-bottomed or non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side, flipping again if needed, until crisp and brown. Cut into quarters and serve. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Upma
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Upma in this source is made with yellow millet rather than semolina.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.229
posts.body_markdown:
Upma in this source is made with yellow millet rather than semolina. Toasting the millet before cooking gives the grain a nutty flavor and helps keep the final texture light.

Mustard seeds are popped in ghee before curry leaves, turmeric, chili, and shallots are cooked. Water and salt are added only after the shallots turn golden.

The toasted millet is whisked into the boiling liquid, then cooked covered over low heat until fluffy. Cilantro or parsley can be added as a simple garnish.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup yellow millet
- 1 tablespoon ghee or olive oil
- 1 tablespoon black mustard seeds
- 5 curry leaves
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- 1/2 cup shallots or onions, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 3 cups water
- Fresh cilantro or parsley, for garnish

## Method
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Spread the millet in a non-stick baking pan and toast for 7–8 minutes until lightly browned. Heat the ghee in a pot over medium-high heat, add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the curry leaves, turmeric, chilies, and shallots, reduce to medium-low, and sauté until the shallots are golden. Add the salt and water, raise the heat, and bring to a boil. Add the toasted millet gradually while stirring constantly. Let the mixture boil for 1–2 minutes, reduce to low, cover, and cook for 25–30 minutes until light and fluffy, adding a little more water near the end if necessary. Garnish and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Carrie’s Spelt Oatmeal Bread
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Carrie’s Spelt Oatmeal Bread combines oats and spelt flour in a yeast-raised loaf with honey, butter, and egg.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.230
posts.body_markdown:
Carrie’s Spelt Oatmeal Bread combines oats and spelt flour in a yeast-raised loaf with honey, butter, and egg. This bread makes two loaves and uses two separate rises.

Boiling water first softens the oats and dissolves the honey, butter, and salt. The yeast is activated separately in warm water before the mixtures are combined and the spelt flour is added.

Spelt is more delicate than common wheat flour, so the source cautions against over-kneading. The baked loaves are brushed with warm honey and sprinkled with oats.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups boiling water
- 1 cup rolled oats
- 1/3 cup honey
- 2 tablespoons butter or ghee
- 2 teaspoons salt
- 1 package active dry yeast, about 1/4 ounce or 8 grams
- 1/2 cup warm water, about 110°F or 43°C
- 1 large egg
- 4 1/2 cups spelt flour
- 2 tablespoons honey, slightly warmed, for brushing
- 2 tablespoons rolled oats, for sprinkling

## Method
Combine the boiling water, oats, honey, butter, and salt in a large bowl and set aside. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let it stand about 10 minutes, then stir it into the oat mixture. Add the egg, then the spelt flour, mixing until a smooth elastic dough forms; add flour a tablespoon at a time if it is too sticky. Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise about 1 hour until doubled. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Punch down the dough, divide in two, shape into loaves, and place in lightly oiled 9-by-5-inch loaf pans. Cover and let rise about 40 minutes until doubled again. Bake about 30 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding underneath. Remove from the pans, brush with warm honey, and sprinkle with oats. Makes 2 loaves, about 10–12 slices each.

posts.title: Spelt Oatmeal Bread: Bread Machine Version
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Spelt Oatmeal Bread: Bread Machine Version | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Spelt Oatmeal Bread: Bread Machine Version simplifies the preceding oatmeal bread into a single-machine loaf.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.231
posts.body_markdown:
Spelt Oatmeal Bread: Bread Machine Version simplifies the preceding oatmeal bread into a single-machine loaf. The oats are still softened with boiling water before the other ingredients are added.

The oat mixture must cool from boiling to warm before the remaining ingredients go into the bread machine. The source leaves the exact ingredient order to the machine manufacturer’s instructions.

The loaf is baked on the light setting. This version keeps the spelt-and-oat character of the original while removing the hand-kneading and separate rise steps.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup old-fashioned oats
- 1 cup boiling water
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 1 1/2 teaspoons salt
- 3 tablespoons honey
- 1 tablespoon dark molasses, optional
- 1 large egg, lightly beaten
- 3 cups light spelt flour
- 2 teaspoons active dry yeast

## Method
Place the old-fashioned oats in the bread machine’s mixing bowl and pour the boiling water over them. Let the oats cool until they are still warm but no longer hot. Add the butter, salt, honey, optional molasses, beaten egg, spelt flour, and yeast in the order recommended by the bread machine manufacturer. Select the light crust setting and bake according to the machine’s program. Makes 1 loaf.

posts.title: Banana Walnut Loaf
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Banana Walnut Loaf is a moist quick bread made with mashed ripe bananas, olive oil, brown sugar, eggs, whole wheat flour, wheat germ, flax, and walnuts.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.232
posts.body_markdown:
Banana Walnut Loaf is a moist quick bread made with mashed ripe bananas, olive oil, brown sugar, eggs, whole wheat flour, wheat germ, flax, and walnuts.

The wet ingredients are mixed only until combined before the dry ingredients are folded in. The source keeps the mixing gentle so the finished loaf does not become tough.

Walnuts are stirred in last, and the loaf bakes until a tester comes out clean. It can be served on its own or alongside fruit.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup olive oil
- 3/4 cup brown sugar, or part gur and part brown sugar
- 2 large eggs
- 1 3/4 cups ripe bananas, mashed
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 1/4 cups whole wheat flour
- 1/4 cup wheat germ
- 1 tablespoon flax seeds, ground
- 1 teaspoon baking soda
- 1 teaspoon baking powder
- 1/4 cup walnuts, chopped

## Method
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). In a large bowl, combine the olive oil, sugar, eggs, mashed bananas, and vanilla and stir until just mixed. Add the whole wheat flour, wheat germ, ground flax seeds, baking soda, and baking powder and fold only until the dry ingredients are moistened. Stir in the chopped walnuts. Pour the batter into a lightly oiled 9-by-5-inch loaf pan and bake for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until a toothpick or fork inserted in the center comes out clean. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Banana, Oat & Berry Muffins
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Banana, Oat & Berry Muffins combine whole wheat flour, cereal or oats, banana, berries, flax, wheat germ.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.233
posts.body_markdown:
Banana, Oat & Berry Muffins combine whole wheat flour, cereal or oats, banana, berries, flax, wheat germ, and a modest amount of oil in a straightforward muffin batter.

The dry ingredients are mixed in one bowl while the egg, oil, banana, sweetener, and milk are combined separately. Bringing the two mixtures together only at the end helps prevent overmixing.

Mixed berries are folded in last. The muffins bake at a relatively hot oven temperature and are cooled on a rack after a clean tester confirms they are done.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/3 cups whole wheat flour
- 1 tablespoon flax seeds, ground
- 2 tablespoons wheat germ
- 1 cup 12-grain cereal or porridge oats
- 2 teaspoons baking powder
- 1 teaspoon baking soda
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1 large egg
- 1/4 cup vegetable oil
- 3/4 cup ripe bananas, mashed
- 1/2 cup sweetener such as brown sugar, maple syrup, or honey
- 3/4 cup milk
- 1/2 cup mixed berries

## Method
Heat the oven to 400°F (205°C). In a large bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, ground flax seeds, wheat germ, cereal or oats, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. In a separate bowl, beat the egg, then mix in the oil, mashed banana, sweetener, and milk. Add the wet mixture to the dry ingredients and stir just until incorporated, then fold in the mixed berries. Lightly oil a muffin tin and divide the batter evenly among the cups. Bake for 18–20 minutes, until a toothpick or fork comes out clean, then cool on a rack. Makes 12 muffins.

posts.title: Sascha’s Blueberry Almond Eggless Muffins
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Sascha’s Blueberry Almond Eggless Muffins | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Sascha’s Blueberry Almond Eggless Muffins use barley flour, soy milk, maple syrup, blueberries, almonds, lemon zest, and vanilla without eggs.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.234
posts.body_markdown:
Sascha’s Blueberry Almond Eggless Muffins use barley flour, soy milk, maple syrup, blueberries, almonds, lemon zest, and vanilla without eggs.

The flour, leaveners, and salt are sifted together first. The liquid ingredients and lemon zest are whisked separately before the blueberries are added.

The wet mixture is combined with the dry ingredients and toasted almonds are stirred in last. The muffins bake quickly and are cooled on a rack before serving.

## Ingredients
- 1 3/4 cups barley flour
- 3/4 teaspoon baking powder
- 1/4 teaspoon baking soda
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon lemon zest, packed
- 7 tablespoons grapeseed or canola oil
- 1/2 cup maple syrup
- 1/2 cup plain soy milk
- 1/2 teaspoon lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 3/4 cup blueberries
- 1/4 cup almonds, peeled, toasted, and roughly chopped

## Method
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Sift the barley flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk the lemon zest, oil, maple syrup, soy milk, lemon juice, and vanilla. Add the blueberries and mix gently. Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and mix until combined, then fold in the toasted almonds. Lightly oil a muffin pan, divide the batter evenly among the cups, and bake for 15–18 minutes, until a toothpick or fork comes out clean. Cool on a rack. Makes 12 muffins.

posts.title: Flax Seed Raintree Crackers
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Flax Seed Raintree Crackers are made with raisins or currants, nuts, mixed seeds, flax, spelt flour, buttermilk, tea, and a small amount of brown sugar.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.235
posts.body_markdown:
Flax Seed Raintree Crackers are made with raisins or currants, nuts, mixed seeds, flax, spelt flour, buttermilk, tea, and a small amount of brown sugar.

These crackers are baked twice. The first bake creates a firm loaf that is refrigerated overnight, making it easier to cut into very thin slices the following day.

The second, lower-temperature bake dries those slices into crisp crackers. They can be stored in an airtight container for an extended period once fully dry.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups raisins or currants
- 3/4 cup mixed chopped nuts, such as almonds or pecans
- 1/4 cup flax seeds
- 1 cup mixed seeds, such as pumpkin, sesame, sunflower, or poppy
- 1 large egg
- 2 tablespoons milk
- 1 cup buttermilk
- 3/4 cup strong black tea, decaf black tea, or rooibos tea
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 cup brown sugar
- 3 1/4 cups plus 2 tablespoons spelt flour
- 2 teaspoons baking soda

## Method
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Combine the raisins, nuts, flax seeds, and mixed seeds in a large bowl. In another bowl, beat the egg and milk, then beat in the buttermilk, tea, salt, and brown sugar. Sift the spelt flour and baking soda over the nut-and-seed mixture, pour in the liquid ingredients, and mix well. Transfer to a lightly oiled pan and bake for 60–75 minutes, until a tester comes out clean. Cover and refrigerate overnight. The next day, heat the oven to 290°F (145°C). Cut the loaf lengthwise into 4 logs, then slice each log very thinly, about 1/4 inch. Arrange on baking sheets and bake about 45 minutes until dry but not browned. Turn off the oven and leave the crackers inside for another 45 minutes to crisp. Store airtight. Makes 60–70 crackers.
